name: Museum St. Anton am Arlberg
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum St. Anton am Arlberg in Trier-Haus: birthplace of alpine skiing, Hannes Schneider's Arlberg technique, and Arlberg railway history.
preis: Erwachsene ca. 6,00 €, Kinder frei (mit St. Anton Sommer-Karte kostenlos)
oeffnungszeiten: Winter tgl. 10:00–18:00 Uhr; Sommer So–Fr 14:00–18:00 Uhr (Sa Ruhetag)
beschreibung:
Overview

The renowned Museum St. Anton am Arlberg (also known as the Ski and Local Heritage Museum St. Anton) is idyllically situated within a tranquil public park overlooking the centre of St. Anton am Arlberg at an elevation of approximately 1,300 metres. Housed within the magnificent Trier-Haus – an Art Nouveau villa completed in 1912 –, the museum is dedicated to the Arlberg's legendary legacy as the "Cradle of Alpine Skiing". Visitors embark on a captivating historical voyage from an impoverished mountain farming enclave through the pioneering construction of the Arlberg Railway to the dawn of modern downhill skiing and premier alpine winter tourism.

Cradle of Skiing & Railway Heritage

St. Anton am Arlberg is internationally revered as the birthplace of modern alpine skiing technique: on 3 January 1901, enthusiastic winter sports pioneers gathered at the historic Hospiz in St. Christoph to establish the legendary Ski-Club Arlberg – among the oldest and most prestigious ski clubs in the world. The museum exhibitions honour ski pioneer Hannes Schneider: on the snowy slopes of the Arlberg, Schneider developed the groundbreaking "Arlberg Technique" (stem turns and parallel skiing), laying the foundation for modern structured ski instruction worldwide through his inaugural ski school. Vintage hickory wooden skis, hand-stitched leather boots, historic 1920s ski films (such as Arnold Fanck's "The White Ecstasy"), and Arlberg-Kandahar trophies bring this golden age vividly to life. A second compelling gallery chronicles alpine transport history: the construction of the Arlberg Railway and its ten-kilometre-long railway tunnel between 1880 and 1884 broke the region's winter isolation and ushered in international leisure travel. The heritage villa also features wood-panelled dining salons hosting an acclaimed restaurant.

Visit & Arrival

The museum is open during the winter season (December to April) daily from 10:00 to 18:00; during the summer season (late June to late September) from Sunday through Friday from 14:00 to 18:00. Admission (2025/2026 season): Adults approx. €6.00, children up to age 14 free; admission is completely free with the regional St. Anton Summer Card. Arrival by rail: St. Anton am Arlberg is the highest-altitude EuroCity and Railjet railway station in the world; from the station it is a pleasant 10-minute walk through the spa park uphill to the museum. By car: Via the Arlberg expressway S16, exit St. Anton am Arlberg; parking is available in town car parks.

Tips

The surrounding park offers a tranquil oasis with a picturesque pond and walking trails; the restaurant terrace in Trier-Haus serves outstanding regional cuisine. Combine your museum visit with a ride on the nearby futuristic Galzigbahn, whose giant Ferris-wheel boarding mechanism continues the tradition of Arlberg cable car engineering.
